first.title: Welcome to ResSwitch
first.text:
ResSwitch is running in the notification area.

Detected native mode: {0}
Left-click the icon (or press {1}) to switch between native and 4:3. Right-click for the menu.

Check for updates at startup? This only reads the latest version number on GitHub and sends no personal data. Nothing is downloaded or installed automatically.
set.title: ResSwitch - Settings
main.intro: One click on the tray icon (or the shortcut) toggles between these two modes:
main.mode1note: Your usual resolution, detected at first launch. Wrong one? Put Windows back on its recommended resolution and click "Use the current mode" (or pick another one above).
main.clickIcon: You can also click the tray icon.
games.empty: No game yet. Start your game, then click "Detect a running game" below.
prof.intro: Create extra resolutions here (for example a different one for each game). They appear in the tray icon menu and in the Games tab.

gpu.nvidia:
To make the 4:3 image fill the whole screen (no black bars):
1. Open the NVIDIA Control Panel (right-click the desktop).
2. Display > Adjust desktop size and position.
3. Scaling mode: "Full-screen", perform scaling on: "GPU".
4. Apply.

If the resolution is missing from the list: Display > Change resolution > Customize > Create custom resolution.

Menu names change between driver versions: this guide is indicative.
gpu.amd:
To make the 4:3 image fill the whole screen (no black bars):
1. Open AMD Software (Adrenalin).
2. Gaming/Settings > Display.
3. Scaling mode: "Full panel" (full screen) and turn "GPU Scaling" on.

Menu names change between driver versions: this guide is indicative.
gpu.intel:
To make the 4:3 image fill the whole screen (no black bars):
1. Open Intel Graphics Command Center.
2. Display > General.
3. Scaling: "Full-screen" (stretch).

Menu names change between driver versions: this guide is indicative.
gpu.generic:
ResSwitch changes the Windows resolution, but stretching the 4:3 image to the whole screen is done by your graphics driver or by your monitor.
Look for a "Scaling" option set to "Full-screen" (or "Stretch") in your graphics driver's control panel, or an "Aspect ratio: Full / Wide" option in your monitor's own menu.

Menu names change between driver versions: this guide is indicative.
